goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:36 — The legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` fallback ignores flex auto-margin alignment, leaving the panel after the title instead of right-aligned in browsers that select it.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real compatibility issue. The diff shows `.panel` uses `margin-left: auto` for right-alignment (line 38), which works with modern flexbox but not with the legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` prefixes in the `@include flexbox()` mixin. The legacy box model doesn't support auto margins for alignment, so in older browsers that use those prefixes, the panel won't be pushed to the right side. This is a verifiable cross-browser compatibility bug introduced by the change from `float: right` to flexbox with auto margins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:263 — Making `.small-action` a flex container disables its button's `float: right`, so action buttons no longer stay at the right edge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `.small-action` is being converted to a flex container with `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)`. The finding correctly identifies that this change would affect any child elements that rely on `float` for positioning. Looking at the diff, there's no corresponding change to handle button positioning within `.small-action`. When a container becomes a flex container, float properties on children are ignored, which could cause buttons that were previously floated right to no longer appear at the right edge. This is a legitimate layout concern that the diff introduces.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117 — The alignment mixin pairs `-moz-box` fallback layout with no `-moz-box-align`, leaving centered content unaligned in legacy Gecko flexbox.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the `@mixin align-items` at line 117 includes `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but does NOT include `-moz-box-align`. Meanwhile, the `@mixin inline-flex()` includes `-moz-box` and `-moz-inline-box` fallbacks. This inconsistency means that in legacy Firefox/Gecko browsers that use the old `-moz-box` flexbox model, the alignment property won't be applied because `-moz-box-align` is missing from the align-items mixin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:17 — The flexbox layout rewrite has no browser or visual regression coverage for header and topic alignment.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a significant layout change from float-based positioning to flexbox in header.scss (removing 'float: left' from .title, removing 'float: right' from .panel, adding flexbox mixins). This is a substantial CSS architecture change that affects visual layout. The finding correctly identifies that this type of layout rewrite could benefit from visual regression testing, as flexbox and float behave differently and could cause alignment issues across browsers. This is a legitimate scope/testing concern for the change, not a bug or hallucination.
